issues.title: __str__ without complementary __repr__
issues.description: The SubscriptionPlan class overrides __str__ without implementing the complementary __repr__ method, violating the requirement that special methods should be properly implemented with their relevant complementary methods
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
class SubscriptionPlan(TypedDict):
    """Tenant subscriptionplan information."""

    plan: str
    expiration_date: int

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        """Return a human-readable string representation for debugging."""
        return f"Plan: {self['plan']}, Expiration: {self['expiration_date']}"
issues.rule_name: Python Code Must Not Override Dunder Methods Unnecessarily

issues.title: Wrong dictionary used in Redis cache pipeline loop
issues.description: In the get_plan_bulk_with_cache method, when caching new tenant plans to Redis, the code iterates over `bulk_plans.items()` instead of `plans_to_cache.items()`. This is problematic because `bulk_plans` may contain tenant plans that had None values from validation failures in get_plan_bulk (when results[tenant_id] = None is set on exception). The code will attempt to cache these None values or invalid entries, leading to corrupted cache data. Additionally, if bulk_plans contains more entries than plans_to_cache due to any filtering logic, the logging statement will report an incorrect count of cached items.

issues.title: Type contract violation in get_plan_bulk return value
issues.description: In the get_plan_bulk method, when subscription plan validation fails for a tenant, the code sets `results[tenant_id] = None` instead of skipping that tenant with `continue`. This violates the method's return type contract of `dict[str, SubscriptionPlan]` by inserting None values. Downstream consumers expecting valid SubscriptionPlan objects will encounter AttributeError or TypeError when attempting to access plan fields like `subscription_plan['plan']` or `subscription_plan['expiration_date']`. This bug can cascade through the caching layer in get_plan_bulk_with_cache, potentially storing None values in Redis.

issues.title: Incorrect cache count in observability logging
issues.description: In the get_plan_bulk_with_cache method, the logging statement reports `len(bulk_plans)` as the number of cached items instead of `len(plans_to_cache)`. This creates misleading observability metrics. When some tenant plans fail validation or are filtered out, bulk_plans will contain more entries than plans_to_cache, causing the log to report an inflated count of successfully cached items. This makes it difficult to diagnose caching issues and can mask problems where fewer plans are actually cached than expected.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
logger.info(
                            "get_plan_bulk_with_cache: cached %s new tenant plans to Redis",
                            len(bulk_plans),
                        )

issues.title: Raising generic Exception instead of domain-specific exception
issues.description: New code raises a generic `Exception` from a service method. Per the rule, backend services should raise domain-specific exceptions (e.g., from `services/errors` or `core/errors`) to provide clearer context and allow consistent translation to HTTP responses.
issues.rule_name: Backend Errors Must Use Domain-Specific Exceptions

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #30339 - feat: get plan bulk with cache
pr.author: unknown

structured_output.summary:
This PR adds `BillingService.get_plan_bulk_with_cache`, which reads tenant subscription plans from Redis in one `mget`, sends only the misses to the billing API through the existing `get_plan_bulk`, and writes the fetched plans back with a pipeline and a 600s TTL. It also changes `get_plan_bulk` so that a tenant whose payload fails validation is recorded individually instead of aborting its whole 200-tenant chunk, and it adds a `__str__` to the `SubscriptionPlan` TypedDict. The Redis fallback paths are well designed: an `mget` failure falls back to the API, and a pipeline failure does not affect the returned data.

The review found a real contract bug. `get_plan_bulk` stores `None` for an invalid tenant, but the new unit test and the docstring both say that tenant should be skipped. That unit test will fail as written. The `None` then flows through `get_plan_bulk_with_cache`, into the typed return value, and into Redis as the string `"null"`. The `__str__` method is dead code, since `TypedDict` instances are plain dicts. `get_plan_bulk_with_cache` has no callers in this PR. I read the code and tests but did not execute the test suite.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The new unit test `test_get_plan_bulk_with_invalid_tenant_plan_skipped` contradicts the implementation: `get_plan_bulk` stores `None` rather than skipping the tenant, so its `len(result) == 2` and `"tenant-invalid" not in result` assertions fail. Also, `None` values leak from `get_plan_bulk` into the `dict[str, SubscriptionPlan]` returned by `get_plan_bulk_with_cache` and get cached as `"null"`. Both must be fixed before merge. The `__str__` addition is dead code and should be removed.

architecture.overview:
Before this PR, `BillingService.get_plan_bulk` is the only bulk path for tenant plans. It POSTs chunks of up to 200 tenant IDs to `/subscription/plan/batch` and validates each returned plan against the `SubscriptionPlan` TypedDict through a pydantic `TypeAdapter`. Nothing caches plans in bulk, so every batch job pays the full billing API cost.

The PR adds a cache-aside layer in front of that path. `get_plan_bulk_with_cache` reads all tenant keys (`tenant_plan:<tenant_id>`) in one Redis `mget`, decodes and validates each hit, and sends only the misses to `get_plan_bulk`. The fetched plans are written back in one pipeline with a 600-second TTL. The validation change in `get_plan_bulk` makes bad entries per-tenant, so one malformed payload no longer drops its whole chunk. Because of that change, the cache path can receive `None` values, which it does not yet handle.
steps: Entry point: `BillingService.get_plan_bulk` in `api/services/billing_service.py` (around line 267). It is unchanged in shape, except that invalid tenant entries are now stored as `None` (line 292) instead of dropping the chunk.
New key and TTL constants sit on `BillingService` (`_PLAN_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX`, `_PLAN_CACHE_TTL = 600`), with `_make_plan_cache_key` building the Redis key.

`get_plan_bulk_with_cache` (around line 304) runs step 1: one `redis_client.mget` over all keys. Hits are decoded from JSON and validated. Malformed hits and misses go to `cache_misses`. An `mget` exception sends every tenant to the API.

Step 2 calls `get_plan_bulk(cache_misses)` and merges the result into `tenant_plans` (lines 362-367). Step 3 writes the results to Redis with `pipeline().setex` (around line 377). A failure there is logged and does not change the return value.

Callers: nothing in the repository calls `get_plan_bulk_with_cache` yet, so the cache path is not exercised outside its tests. The tests are an integration suite against real Redis and a unit test for the `get_plan_bulk` validation change.

findings.title: Invalid tenant plans are stored as None, contradicting the test and docstring
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/services/billing_service.py`, `get_plan_bulk` (around lines 284-292) stores `None` for tenants whose plan fails `subscription_adapter.validate_python`. That violates the `dict[str, SubscriptionPlan]` return type and conflicts with the unit test `test_get_plan_bulk_with_invalid_tenant_plan_skipped` in `api/tests/unit_tests/services/test_billing_service.py` (around lines 1297-1331), which expects the invalid tenant to be omitted. Change the except branch so it logs and does not add the tenant to `results`, which matches the test and the existing `continue` style in the outer handler. Keep the per-tenant logging. Then confirm that `get_plan_bulk_with_cache` never sees `None` values (see the related finding on cache writes).

findings.title: None values leak into the cache path's return value and get cached as "null"
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/services/billing_service.py`, `get_plan_bulk_with_cache` (around lines 361-385) copies every value from `bulk_plans` into `tenant_plans` and the Redis write, including `None` entries that `get_plan_bulk` can return. Filter out `None` values before the merge and before the pipeline write, so only validated `SubscriptionPlan` dicts reach the return value and Redis. Also remove the redundant `plans_to_cache` dict and write directly from the filtered `bulk_plans`. Keep the existing log message and the try/except around the pipeline. Match the existing style of the function.

findings.title: __str__ on the SubscriptionPlan TypedDict never runs
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/services/billing_service.py`, remove the `__str__` method from the `SubscriptionPlan` TypedDict (around lines 28-30). Methods do not work in a TypedDict body, and instances are plain dicts, so this method never runs. Do not add a replacement unless a call site needs a readable format. If one is needed, put it in a helper function near the call site.

findings.title: get_plan_bulk_with_cache is unused in this PR
findings.body:
No production code calls `get_plan_bulk_with_cache`. Only tests exercise it. This is fine if a follow-up PR wires it into a batch job, but reviewers should know that the Redis cache, the 600s TTL, and the consistency trade-off have no production effect yet. The docstring already says that callers wanting high consistency should use `get_plan_bulk`.

::diff{file="api/services/billing_service.py" lines="304-313"}
findings.fixPrompt: Confirm with the author whether `BillingService.get_plan_bulk_with_cache` in `api/services/billing_service.py` is meant to ship before its caller. If it is, note the intended caller in the PR description. If not, consider deferring the function to the PR that adds the caller.

findings.title: Empty-input test makes no assertion about Redis
findings.body:
`test_get_plan_bulk_with_cache_empty_tenant_ids` checks the return value and the API mock. Its trailing comments say the Redis `mget` call cannot be verified and then stop. The test therefore cannot catch a regression where an empty input triggers a Redis round trip, and it looks more complete than it is. Either patch `redis_client.mget` and assert it was not called, or remove the misleading comments.

::diff{file="api/tests/test_containers_integration_tests/services/test_billing_service.py" lines="304-316"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/tests/test_containers_integration_tests/services/test_billing_service.py`, `test_get_plan_bulk_with_cache_empty_tenant_ids` (around lines 304-316) has comments saying it cannot verify that Redis is not called, and it does not test that. Patch `redis_client.mget` with `patch.object` and assert it was not called, then remove the misleading comment. Keep the existing assertions on the return value and the API mock.

findings.title: Good fallback design on Redis failures
findings.body: The cache path degrades in the right order. An `mget` exception or a length mismatch sends every tenant to the billing API. A malformed cached value becomes a miss for that tenant only. A failed pipeline write is logged and does not affect the returned data. The integration tests cover each of these branches against real Redis, and the TTL-expiry test checks that the key is absent before the call.

findings.title: Staleness trade-off is documented
findings.body: The 10-minute TTL means a plan change can take up to ten minutes to appear in batch results. The `get_plan_bulk_with_cache` docstring says this and points high-consistency callers to `get_plan_bulk`. That is an acceptable trade-off for batch jobs, but any caller that gates access on plan state should not use the cached path.
